heading: INT. RETIREMENT HOME RECREATION HALL - DAY

units.text: INT. RETIREMENT HOME RECREATION HALL - DAY
A long room with a linoleum floor the color of weak tea.
A bingo cage in one corner, a folding table of sad cookies in another.
On the wall, a banner reads "SPRING FLING" and has read so since the previous spring.
Three people occupy the room.
MAXINE "MAX" OKONKWO-BELL, 70s, a retired stunt performer in a velvet tracksuit, sits at the center table with a deck of cards fanned in one hand.
Beside her, a dozing oxygen tank on wheels and a bowl of butterscotch.
Across from her, her grandson DESMOND, 20s, thin, pressed shirt, a lanyard that says VISITOR, reads a text message with his thumb stuck in his mouth.

And by the cookie table, hunched over a tray, is the nurse's aide FLORENCE "FLO" ABERNATHY, 50s, teal scrubs, hair under a net, who has been listening to the whole room for years and revealing nothing.
A phone on the wall buzzes.
Nobody answers it.
It buzzes again.
Desmond, your telephone is ringing.
units.name: MAX

units.text: It's a text, Nana.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: That's the wall phone.
units.name: MAX

units.text: Oh.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: He glances at it.
It buzzes.
He looks at Max, who raises one eyebrow so high it nearly leaves her face.
He sighs, crosses the room, and lifts the receiver.
Flo watches him.
Max shuffles.
The cards ride a bridge, snap, and settle.
Desmond holds the phone out from his ear as a voice squawks.
Good morning, Mr. Okonkwo-Bell. Your grandmother has a delivery.
units.name: FRONT DESK

units.text: My grandmother has a what?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: A delivery. Two men are bringing it up.
units.name: FRONT DESK

units.text: Nana, what did you order?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Nothing.
units.name: MAX

units.text: They say it's a delivery.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Then it's a surprise. Hang up.
units.name: MAX

units.text: It's from the front desk.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Then hang up on the front desk.
units.name: MAX

units.text: He hangs up.
At once the double doors swing open and two movers in blue coveralls wheel in a crate the size of a refrigerator, strapped to a hand truck.
They park it in the middle of the floor.
Without a word they unstrap it, tip it forward, and peel away the cardboard.
Beneath is a vintage motorcycle, gleaming chrome, a leather jacket draped across the seat.
Desmond walks around it twice.
Flo sets down her tray.
Max does not rise.
Nana.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Hm?
units.name: MAX

units.text: Is this yours?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Was.
units.name: MAX

units.text: Nana, you said you sold it in 1994.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: I said a lot of things in 1994.
units.name: MAX

units.text: Flo approaches the bike, runs a thumb along the handlebar, and glances back at Max.
Miss Max, it's not on the activity calendar.
units.name: FLO

units.text: Flo, I will tell you what's on my calendar.
units.name: MAX

units.text: You're due for your pills at noon.
units.name: FLO

units.text: My calendar says I'm due for a ride at noon.
units.name: MAX

units.text: You cannot ride it.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: I can sit on it.
units.name: MAX

units.text: You can't sit on it either. Dr. Pruitt specifically--
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Dr. Pruitt isn't here, and the man on the bike, in the photograph over there, was the best looking thing in the state of Ohio.
units.name: MAX

units.text: She nods at a framed photograph on the wall, a younger Max in a leather jacket mid-leap over a line of cars.
Desmond looks at the photograph, then at the bike, then at the movers, who have stepped back and are clutching a clipboard.
Who sent this?
units.name: FLO

units.text: Sign here, ma'am.
units.name: MOVER

units.text: Who's the sender?
units.name: FLO

units.text: It says "Harlan."
units.name: MOVER

units.text: Max's hand stops on the cards.
The room goes quiet.
A small, amused crinkle appears at the corner of her eye, then spreads.
That son of a gun.
units.name: MAX

units.text: Who's Harlan?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Your grandfather's brother. He died in the spring.
units.name: MAX

units.text: Then who sent it?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: He did, Desmond. He did. He always said he'd send me something nice when he got where he was going.
units.name: MAX

units.text: She gets up.
She walks to the bike.
Flo hurries to steady the oxygen tank on its wheels.
Max lays her hand on the seat and strokes it with two fingers.
Desmond. Fetch the helmet.
units.name: MAX

units.text: There's a helmet?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: There's always a helmet.
units.name: MAX

units.text: He lifts the leather jacket and finds one beneath it.
He holds it out.
Max puts it on, buckles the strap, and swings a leg over the seat with a fluency that stops everyone's breath.
Miss Max.
units.name: FLO

units.text: Flo, if you tell Dr. Pruitt, I'll haunt you.
units.name: MAX

units.text: He'll see the tank.
units.name: FLO

units.text: Then I'll leave the tank.
units.name: MAX

units.text: She unhooks the oxygen tube, hands it to Flo, and grips the handlebars.
Desmond covers his face with both hands.
Flo stares at the tube.
The bike does not start.
It doesn't have a key.
Max grins, rests her forehead against the tank, and begins to laugh until the laughing turns to a wheeze, then a cough.
Flo is at her side in an instant with the tube.
Breathe, Miss Max.
units.name: FLO

units.text: I am. I am. I'm breathing.
units.name: MAX

units.text: Nana.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Desmond, I want to sit here for a minute.
units.name: MAX

units.text: He pulls a chair beside the bike and sits.
Flo sits on the other side.
Max rests her hands on the handlebars, eyes closed, and for a while none of them says anything.
The movers back out of the room.
